solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plant after day is OK

indicators.note: after places the plant's word behind the day and 'is' in the answer

parts.note: Sat is the standard short form of Saturday
a plant is an industrial works, a factory

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a houseplant is doing fine now that a day has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like greenery, but it is the industrial kind. The clue gives the pieces in reverse order; 'after' tells you to put the plant last.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for something adequate, acceptable or good enough.

clue.text: Wonderful agent takes us up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the combined letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent for a firm

explanation.surface: A marvellous secret agent gives us a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' just joins REP and US; 'up' then reverses the whole string REPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal synonym for excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Very sensitive poets roaming over island, endlessly

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the shuffled poets above the shortened island
roaming means wandering about, so the letters of poets are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the island's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: Wandering poets travel across an island without end, carrying something highly confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaming' turns POETS into TOPSE; 'endlessly' cuts CRETE to CRET; 'over' stacks TOPSE on CRET.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified material that is extremely sensitive is labelled top secret.

clue.text: Great Depression: 'flu spreading?

indicators.note: a spreading illness scatters, so the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deep depression is blamed on influenza going round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Depression' reads as the 1930s slump, but 'Great' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendiferous is a jocular, inflated word for splendid or magnificent.

clue.text: Old weapons in unopened graves

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its first letter, as if its door were never opened

parts.note: barrows are ancient burial mounds, prehistoric graves

explanation.surface: Ancient arms are found inside burial sites nobody has excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: Bows and their projectiles were the weaponry of earlier ages, long before firearms.

clue.text: Bouncers spit: mortal sin, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of these words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nightclub doormen are told that spitting is a grave sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncers' suggests club doormen, but here it means people who bounce for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasts who leap on a sprung mat are literally people who bounce.

clue.text: Rubbish peak to climb

indicators.note: in a down clue, to climb means the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Litter is strewn on a summit that hikers are trying to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR, a rocky hill in south-west England, is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot means nonsense, as in 'talking rot'.

clue.text: Produce book, penning ultimate in ghoulish twist

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: to produce a book is to write it

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the final letter of ghoulish

explanation.surface: An author writes a novel with a ghoulish plot twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, chiming with 'Produce book', but it means enclosing: H goes inside WRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, as in pain.

clue.text: Companion welcoming secretary of a RC leader

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching an adjective

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pal is a friend or companion
PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: A friend invites the secretary of a Catholic leader inside.
explanation.walkthrough: RC is the standard abbreviation for Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Papal describes anything belonging to the Pope, head of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Roll filled with a fowl for the oven

indicators.note: filled with means the word has something put inside it

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster

explanation.surface: A bread roll is stuffed with chicken ready for cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' suggests bread, but it is a list: A goes inside ROSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaster is a chicken bred to be cooked whole in the oven.

clue.text: Grass over lovely Cambridge Backs

indicators.note: backs means the ends of each word, so the last letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: Grass grows across the lovely lawns of the Backs in Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Backs are the riverside lawns behind Cambridge colleges; here 'Backs' takes the last letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal plant, and cereals are grasses.

clue.text: Latest run for paper

parts.note: the latest thing is new
a sprint is a fast run

explanation.surface: The most recent print run goes to the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap paper that newspapers are printed on.

clue.text: Popular icon got dressed up in disguise

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: dressed up means put in fancy dress, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous celebrity put on a costume to go unrecognised.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito describes someone hiding their identity, travelling under cover.

clue.text: Dog carried back by big rocket

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
carried by means held within the words that follow, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dog is sent up on a large rocket, like the early space dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Dog carried' as the definition, but 'carried' signals the hidden letters ('carried ... by'), so 'Dog' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Something flashing across the sky, then nothing: regain consciousness

parts.note: a comet streaks across the night sky
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sees a streak in the sky, then blacks out and later wakes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is a phrasal verb meaning to recover from fainting.

clue.text: Caught in trap, illicit profit made

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the trap's word

parts.note: a lure is a bait or trap
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A criminal snared in a sting is found to have made dirty money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre, as in 'filthy lucre', is money gained dishonourably.

clue.text: Tenacious horse: famous name carrying you

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a star is a celebrity, a famous name
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A dogged racehorse with a big name carries you to victory.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a horse with stamina for long distances is called a stayer.

clue.text: Old article in complex meant to be shabby

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation and the article inside the jumbled word
complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of meant are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An old piece of writing in a building complex was supposed to look worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' turns MEANT into MATEN; 'in' puts OTHE after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing eaten by moths is worn, tatty and threadbare.

clue.text: Musical performance that may go either way?

definitions.meaning: a booking for a band to play live
cryptically, a word that reads identically forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: A concert whose outcome is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may go either way' sounds like an uncertain result, but it describes a word reading the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a concert or live booking for a band, and its letters form a palindrome.

clue.text: Politician needing info about Religious Education

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A politician needs briefing on school religious teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Green Party, an environmentalist political party, is a Green.

clue.text: Attempt to nail one record in series of three

indicators.note: to nail means to fasten in, so the pieces are fixed inside the attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral for one
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone tries for a record in a three-part series.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilogy is a set of three related books, films or plays.

clue.text: Something cold seen during Antarctic expedition

indicators.note: seen during means visible within the following words, which hold the letters

explanation.surface: Something cold is spotted on a polar expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is frozen water, the coldest thing in the Antarctic.

clue.text: Heard of charming apartment!

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: sweet means delightful or charming

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims they have heard of a delightful flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite is a set of connected rooms, as in a hotel.

clue.text: Stirring espresso, don't — use this?

indicators.note: stirring means mixing around, so the letters of the two words are churned up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Advice not to stir your coffee with this rather large spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a wry description: a big spoon is too large for a tiny espresso cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessertspoon is a mid-sized spoon for puddings, too big for stirring coffee.
